plan_summary: Give the terminal failure-reason vocabulary an explicit severity split, sourced from the classification execution-report.js already computes. Four files change, all inside policy.allowed_paths. (1) adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js gains one new closed-enum reason string, EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH, added to both NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS; a pure classifier severityForReason(reason) derived from exactly those two existing sets (non-retriable when a member of either, retriable otherwise, null for no reason) exported from module.exports; an additive report field failure_reason_severity beside failure_reason in execution_report.json plus one matching line in the Markdown render; and a SCHEMA_VERSION bump 1.4.0 -> 1.5.0 documented in the file's existing additive-change comment block. decideLifecycle's branches, its decision_reason strings, the DECISIONS/GATE_STATUSES vocabularies, the exit codes, and the CLI stdout line are all left byte-identical -- the new reason is a brand-new string no existing fixture carries, so no fixture's decision or exit code can move. (2) adws-pipeline/references/phase-gates.md keeps its 'Failure-reason classes' H2 heading verbatim (SKILL.md, which is outside allowed_paths, cross-references that heading by name) and replaces the two-bullet class list under it with a single reason table whose columns carry the severity: Reason | Terminal severity | Verdict class | In-run retry | Emitted by / note. Every reason gets a row -- CREDENTIAL_FAILURE, OPERATOR_CANCEL, MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT, PLAN_COHERENCE_BELOW_THRESHOLD, ADVOCATE_DISSENT, the new EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH, PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED, PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK, STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and the {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE family -- with a precedence rule that a named reason always wins and {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE is the default only when no named reason applies, a sourcing rule that the severity column transcribes severityForReason() and the orchestrator reads execution_report.json.failure_reason_severity rather than parsing gate detail prose, and an explicit note that ADVOCATE_DISSENT_REPAIRED and CRITIC_FAIL_REPAIRED are attempt-level annotations that never enter this table. The same file's consensus uphold path and the evidence-integrity path are pinned to their named reasons. (3) adws-pipeline/references/artifact-layout.md states that run_manifest.failure_reason is a closed enum defined by that table and names EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH as the terminal reason for the skill_trace transcription breach it already describes. (4) adws-pipeline/references/troubleshooting.md gains a one-line pointer from its existing '{PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE' triage note to the severity table. Existing recorded reasons keep their current meaning: PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED stays no-retry-in-run but retriable-at-terminal, and PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK keeps its documented quarantine-on-second-BLOCK behaviour, both stated in the table's note column rather than redefined. Two out-of-scope consequences are recorded for the orchestrator rather than acted on: editing shipped skill files invalidates the sha256 digests in adws-pipeline/skill-manifest.json (not in allowed_paths -- the Tier-1 local-ci manifest-currency assert will flag it until an operator regenerates it), and the parity corpus under parity/ (blocked for writes) must be RUN unmodified to prove decisions and exit codes are unchanged.

file_change_proposal.description: Four additive edits, no behaviour change for any existing reason string. (a) Add the closed-enum reason 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH' to NO_RETRY_REASONS and to QUARANTINE_REASONS (lines 53-61), so a run the orchestrator terminates for an unreadable-evidence or trace/validator-mismatch breach classifies as non-retriable/quarantine-class instead of falling through decideLifecycle's default RETRY branch. It is a new string, so no existing fixture's decision or exit code can move. (b) Add a pure classifier severityForReason(reason) -> 'non-retriable' | 'retriable' | null, defined ONLY over the two existing sets (member of either -> non-retriable; any other recorded reason -> retriable; non-string/null -> null). This is exactly the classification decideLifecycle already applies at lines 900-918 -- it introduces no third source of truth and no new set. (c) In buildReport's report object (around line 1386) emit failure_reason_severity: severityForReason(failureReason) immediately after failure_reason, and add one line to the Markdown header block (after '- **Failure reason:**', around line 1103) rendering it, so an operator and an orchestrator both read severity as a field rather than re-deriving it from gate detail prose. (d) Bump SCHEMA_VERSION '1.4.0' -> '1.5.0' and extend the existing versioned comment block above it in the same style, recording that 1.5.0 adds the failure_reason_severity field and the EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH reason, additive, with no new gate key, no new DECISION, and no new exit code. Export severityForReason from module.exports beside NO_RETRY_REASONS/QUARANTINE_REASONS. Explicitly DO NOT touch: decideLifecycle's branch structure or its decision_reason strings, DECISIONS, GATE_STATUSES, exitCodeFor, the gates array or any gate key, and the CLI stdout line at the end of main() (parity/cli-contract pins that line and the exit-code contract).

The reference that owns the terminal reason vocabulary. Keep the H2 heading 'Failure-reason classes (port of `phases.js` reason sets)' byte-identical -- SKILL.md line 391 cross-references it by name and SKILL.md is outside allowed_paths -- and replace the two bullets at lines 459-471 with one table that defines every reason and states its severity in the same row: columns Reason | Terminal severity (retriable / non-retriable) | Verdict class (RETRY / QUARANTINE) | In-run retry | Emitted by / note. Rows: CREDENTIAL_FAILURE, OPERATOR_CANCEL, MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT, PLAN_COHERENCE_BELOW_THRESHOLD (reserved), ADVOCATE_DISSENT, EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH (new), PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED, PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK, STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and the {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE family with its seven expansions. Add beneath the table: (i) a SOURCING rule -- the Terminal severity column transcribes execution-report.js's severityForReason(), i.e. membership of NO_RETRY_REASONS union QUARANTINE_REASONS, and the orchestrator reads execution_report.json.failure_reason_severity; it never re-derives severity by parsing a gate's detail string; (ii) a PRECEDENCE rule -- when a named reason in the table applies, it is recorded, and {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE is the default only when none does (this is what stops the flattening SKILL.md line 265-267 leaves as a judgement call); (iii) an explicit evidence-integrity rule -- a skills_clean FAIL caused by unreadable evidence or a skill_trace/validator verdict mismatch (including one found in a superseded attempt) terminates on EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH, never on {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE; (iv) a preservation note that PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED stays no-retry-in-run yet retriable at terminal, and PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK keeps its existing second-BLOCK quarantine behaviour -- stated, not redefined; (v) a note that ADVOCATE_DISSENT_REPAIRED and CRITIC_FAIL_REPAIRED are attempt-level annotations that never reach run_manifest.failure_reason and have no row. Also: extend the Contents line 11 to mention the severity column; and at the consensus uphold bullet (line 371-373) plus the unresolved-dissent sentence (line 322) state that the terminal reason is ADVOCATE_DISSENT -- non-retriable per the table -- and MUST NOT be recorded as REVIEW_GATE_FAILURE or TEST_GATE_FAILURE.

Bind the evidence schema to the new table. At the run_manifest.json shape notes (lines 60-68, where final_status's enum is already spelled out) add that failure_reason is likewise a CLOSED enum -- its values and their retriable/non-retriable severity are defined in references/phase-gates.md 'Failure-reason classes'; free text is never a terminal reason. At the skill_trace transcription rule (lines 391-400), where the breach is currently described only as 'an evidence-integrity breach, the same class as MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT', name the terminal reason: the orchestrator records EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH (non-retriable), keeping the existing same-class wording so the reason's meaning is added, not redefined. No shape key is added or removed, so tolerant-reader/strict-writer rule 8 is untouched.

One-line cross-reference for the operator doing triage. The existing rule at line 45-47 ('Never record an infrastructure death as a `{PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE`') is the place a reader first meets the blanket reason; append a pointer that the full reason vocabulary, and whether a given reason is retriable or non-retriable, is the table in references/phase-gates.md 'Failure-reason classes' -- so the reader who must decide retry-vs-quarantine is sent to the severity column instead of inferring it from gate detail prose. No existing guidance is changed.

criteria_map.criterion: The terminal failure reason vocabulary documents, for every reason, whether that reason is retriable or non-retriable, and the severity is stated in the same table the reason is defined in.
criteria_map.check_idea: Executable doc/code cross-check, run from the repo root: parse the Markdown table under the 'Failure-reason classes' heading of adws-pipeline/references/phase-gates.md, and assert (1) every data row has a non-empty Terminal severity cell whose value is exactly 'retriable' or 'non-retriable'; (2) the set of reasons the table marks non-retriable equals the union of NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS require()d from adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js; (3) every literal reason string appearing elsewhere in adws-pipeline/references/ and in execution-report.js (ADVOCATE_DISSENT, PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK, STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED, {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE, ...) has a row, and the attempt-only annotations ADVOCATE_DISSENT_REPAIRED / CRITIC_FAIL_REPAIRED have none. Falsifiability baseline: run the identical script against the pre-change file materialized with `git show main:adws-pipeline/references/phase-gates.md` into the tester's scratch root -- it must go RED with assertion-failed-runtime-present (there is no table on main, only a two-bullet class list), not with a collection error.

criteria_map.criterion: An upheld advocate dissent terminates on a distinct non-retriable failure reason rather than on the blanket phase gate failure reason.
criteria_map.check_idea: Two-part check. Doc: assert the consensus uphold bullet in phase-gates.md names ADVOCATE_DISSENT as the terminal reason and explicitly forbids recording REVIEW_GATE_FAILURE / TEST_GATE_FAILURE for it, and that the table row for ADVOCATE_DISSENT reads non-retriable. Runtime: build a synthetic evidence tree in the tester's scratch root (run_manifest.json with final_status 'failed', failure_reason 'ADVOCATE_DISSENT', plus a review attempt whose consensus/advocate.json carries a dissent with resolution.action 'uphold'), run `node adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js <dir>`, and assert exit code 2, decision QUARANTINE, and execution_report.json.failure_reason_severity === 'non-retriable' -- while the same tree with failure_reason 'REVIEW_GATE_FAILURE' reports 'retriable', proving the two are now distinguishable without reading any gate detail string. Baseline: the same runtime assertion against the pre-change script goes RED because failure_reason_severity does not exist.

criteria_map.criterion: An evidence integrity breach terminates on a distinct non-retriable failure reason rather than on the blanket phase gate failure reason.
criteria_map.check_idea: Runtime check on the reason's classification: synthesize an evidence tree in scratch whose run_manifest.json records final_status 'failed' and failure_reason 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH' (with a skills/{id}/skill_trace.json whose rubric_result disagrees with its own output.rubric_result, so the skills_clean gate independently FAILs for the documented reason), run the CLI, and assert exit code 2, decision QUARANTINE, decision_reason naming the quarantine/non-retriable class, and failure_reason_severity 'non-retriable'. Falsifiability baseline: the identical tree scored by the pre-change script (`git archive main` into scratch) must go RED for the right reason -- the unknown reason falls through to the RETRY branch, giving decision RETRY and exit code 1. Doc side: assert phase-gates.md states the breach terminates on EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH and never on {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE, and that artifact-layout.md's skill_trace rule names the same reason.

criteria_map.criterion: The severity of a terminal failure reason is sourced from the classification execution-report.js already computes, not re-derived by an orchestrator parsing gate detail strings.
criteria_map.check_idea: Assert the single source. (1) require() adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js and check severityForReason is an exported function; for every reason in the phase-gates table assert severityForReason(reason) equals that row's severity cell, and that severityForReason is defined purely over NO_RETRY_REASONS/QUARANTINE_REASONS -- static check: the function body references only those two sets and no gate, detail, or reason-prose string (grep the function body for 'detail'/'reason:'/'gates' and require zero hits). (2) Assert execution_report.json carries failure_reason_severity and execution_report.md renders it, so the orchestrator has a field to read. (3) Negative grep over adws-pipeline/references/ for any instruction to infer severity from a gate's detail text -- must be zero, and phase-gates.md must carry the explicit prohibition. (4) Regression, satisfying the parity constraint: run the corpora unmodified and read-only -- `node parity/run-parity.js`, `node parity/execution-report-fixtures/run-tests.js` (25 fixtures), `node parity/cli-contract/run-tests.js` -- and require identical decision and exit code to the pre-change baseline for every fixture; parity/ is a blocked path, so it is executed, never edited. Baseline: severityForReason does not exist on main, so (1) goes RED with a runtime assertion failure.
